title: Guardian Pharmacy Services forecasts $123M-$127M adjusted EBITDA amid ira pricing reset
content:
Earnings Call Insights: Guardian Pharmacy Services (GRDN) Q1 2026

MANAGEMENT VIEW

 	*
CEO Fred Burke said this was the company’s “first full quarter operating under the new IRA framework,” and that “for our book of business, we experienced an approximately 60% decline in pricing across our branded drug mix that was impacted by the IRA,” while also reporting that “we were able to deliver a 2% increase year-over-year in reported revenue.”

 	*
Burke said mitigation actions offset the expected profitability impact: “Absent our mitigation efforts, the IRA would have represented approximately a $10 million headwind,” and “those efforts were realized in the quarter, allowing us to deliver double-digit gross profit growth.”

 	*
Burke highlighted cash-cycle complexity and working-capital pressure from the new Medicare Transaction Facilitator, including that the IRA created “a onetime working capital reset,” which he said was “fully within our capacity to manage given the strength of our balance sheet.”

 	*
CFO David Morris summarized operating momentum and the quarter’s scale metrics: “Total residents increased 10% year-over-year to approximately 207,000,” and “script volumes were also strong, increasing 10% year-over-year.”

 	*
Morris also flagged the quarter’s capital markets activity: “The offering was for 6.9 million Class A shares... and was priced at $31 a share,” and added, “today, we filed a new shelf registration statement... At this time, we do not have any plans to utilize the shelf.”

OUTLOOK

 	*
Management reiterated full-year revenue guidance and raised adjusted EBITDA guidance tied to discrete Q1 benefits. Burke said, “we’re updating our full year adjusted EBITDA guidance to include the $3 million benefit recognized in the quarter,” and guided to “$123 million to $127 million, up from $120 million to $124 million,” while “revenue guidance remains at $1.4 billion (sic) [ $1.40 billion ] to $1.42 billion.”

 	*
Burke described cost items embedded in the unchanged underlying view: “our underlying outlook for the business remains unchanged,” while “fuel... can represent a headwind of up to a few million dollars annually if prices remain elevated,” and “labor costs are likely to trend modestly higher over the remainder of the year.”

 	*
Compared with the prior quarter, the revenue range was reiterated and adjusted EBITDA guidance was increased. In Q4, Burke said the company was “raising our 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $120 million to $124 million” and “maintaining our current revenue forecast of $1.4 billion to $1.42 billion,” versus Q1’s updated adjusted EBITDA range of $123 million to $127 million and the same revenue range.

FINANCIAL RESULTS

 	*
Morris reported revenue of “$336.6 million,” and said “reported revenue was up 2%,” adding, “absent the government-mandated price declines from the IRA, revenues would have been up low double digits year-over-year.”

 	*
Profitability was led by gross profit and margin expansion. Morris said, “gross profit was $76 million, up 19% year-over-year,” and “reported gross margin was 22.7%,” while “excluding the $3 million benefit, gross margin was 22%.”

 	*
On costs and one-time items, Morris said, “this quarter includes a $3.2 million legal expense,” and “subsequent to quarter end, we reached a settlement... resulting in an $8.5 million cash payment that will be recognized as other income in the second quarter and will not be included in our adjusted EBITDA.”

 	*
Morris reported, “adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $29.8 million,” and “adjusted EPS was $0.29 per share,” while also noting acquisition integration pressure: “acquisitions... are collectively contributing modest profitability... dampening margins by approximately 80 basis points.”

 	*
On liquidity and IRA working capital, Morris said, “cash ended the quarter at $65 million,” and “approximately half of the working capital used in the quarter was attributable to the IRA,” which he described as “a temporary timing shift rather than a structural change.”

Q&A

 	*
Brian Tanquilut, Jefferies: asked about capital allocation and deal pipeline; CEO Burke responded, “we have a very robust M&A pipeline” and “we intend to maintain the pace that you’ve seen recently.”

 	*
Tanquilut, Jefferies: asked about senior housing occupancy dynamics; CEO Burke said, “Q1 is generally for the industry, a challenge,” and added, “the underlying drivers remain absolutely intact... we’ve got the silver tsunami occurring before our very eyes.”

 	*
John Ransom, Raymond James: asked how legal expense and the “$3 million good guy” flowed through adjusted EBITDA; CFO Morris answered, “the $3.2 million of legal is added back,” and “the $3 million good guy is included.”

 	*
Ransom, Raymond James: asked whether IRA negotiations were a “win, a tie or a loss” with PBMs and about value-based reimbursement; CEO Burke said payor discussions were “very, very positive and constructive,” and “we do have several things underway with respect to value-based reimbursement.”

 	*
Allen Lutz, BofA Securities: asked whether smaller competitors’ IRA strain is changing acquisition conversations; CFO Morris said, “I would say no dramatic shift, and it’s sort of early.”

 	*
Lutz, BofA Securities: asked what’s embedded in updated EBITDA guidance versus fuel/labor risk; CEO Burke said, “our guidance includes our... ability to overcome the fuel headwind, but we’ll have to be watching that carefully.”

 	*
Raj Kumar, Stephens: asked whether the acquisition-related margin drag persists in guidance; CFO Morris said, “whether it’s 80 basis points, 90, 70... we see that trending on into ’26 and ’27.”

SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

 	*
Analysts’ tone was slightly positive and implementation-focused, with repeated probing on guidance quality, IRA second-order effects, and M&A pacing, including Ransom’s framing around IRA outcomes (“a win, a tie or a loss”) and Lutz’s question on competitor distress translating into deal urgency.

 	*
Management’s tone in prepared remarks was confident on IRA execution but cautious on cost volatility, with Burke stating, “I can now say with confidence and clarity that the business performed in line with our expectations,” while also emphasizing discipline given “potential fuel cost pressures.”

 	*
Versus Q4, the tone shifted from year-end outperformance framing to operational validation of IRA mechanics; Q4 emphasized results “ahead of plan,” while Q1 emphasized that “pricing is flowing through as we forecasted” and that new processes are “functional.”

QUARTER-OVER-QUARTER COMPARISON

 	*
The central narrative moved from preparing for IRA and describing monitoring plans in Q4 to reporting realized IRA impacts and mitigation results in Q1, including Burke’s Q1 disclosure of an “approximately 60% decline in pricing” on impacted branded drugs.

 	*
Guidance language stayed conservative in both quarters about nonrecurring items, with Q1 again flagging variability: “items such as these cannot be forecasted as recurring,” while Q4 similarly said favorable variability was “not” projected into the base.

 	*
Analysts’ focus expanded from durability of Q4 upside and IRA contracting (Q4) to working capital, guidance composition, and whether competitor pressure is accelerating M&A (Q1).

RISKS AND CONCERNS

 	*
Burke highlighted ongoing uncertainty around legislative relief: “we view the likelihood of any near-term action as uncertain at best,” despite “discussion around potential legislative relief, including a bipartisan bill proposing a dispensing fee.”

 	*
Burke cited fuel volatility risk: “there is potential for continued volatility,” and said it “can represent a headwind of up to a few million dollars annually if prices remain elevated.”

 	*
Morris pointed to acquisition integration as a continuing margin headwind, stating recent acquisitions remain “well below our consolidated margin profile,” while also indicating the IRA transition drove a temporary working-capital impact.

FINAL TAKEAWAY

Management presented Q1 as a proof point that IRA pricing declines and new payment mechanics are tracking as modeled, with mitigation actions supporting higher full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $123 million to $127 million while maintaining revenue guidance of $1.40 billion to $1.42 billion. The call also emphasized a robust acquisition pipeline, a temporary IRA-related working-capital reset viewed as manageable, and near-term watch items around fuel and labor costs, alongside ongoing uncertainty on legislative relief and the evolving competitive landscape.

title: Stevanato Group (STVN) Reports Next Week: Wall Street Expects Earnings Growth
content:
Wall Street expects a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when Stevanato Group (STVN) reports results for the quarter ended March 2026. While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on May 7. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call will mostly determine the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations, it's worth having a handicapping insight into the odds of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This maker of glass vials for COVID-19 vaccines is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.12 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +9.1%.

Revenues are expected to be $311.41 million, up 15.4% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change.

Price, Consensus and EPS SurprisePrice, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for STVN

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Stevanato?

For Stevanato, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -1.64%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #4.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Stevanato will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Stevanato would post earnings of $0.2 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.21, delivering a surprise of +5.00%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Stevanato doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

Expected Results of an Industry Player

Guardian Pharmacy Services (GRDN), another stock in the Zacks Medical - Drugs industry, is expected to report earnings per share of $0.24 for the quarter ended March 2026. This estimate points to a year-over-year change of +14.3%. Revenues for the quarter are expected to be $329.68 million, up 0.1% from the year-ago quarter.

The consensus EPS estimate for Guardian Pharmacy has remained unchanged over the last 30 days. However, an equal Most Accurate Estimate has resulted in an Earnings ESP of 0.00%.

This Earnings ESP, combined with its Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Guardian Pharmacy will beat the consensus EPS estimate. Over the last four quarters, the company surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times.

title: Bet on Winning DuPont Analysis & Pick 5 Top Stocks
content:
Return on equity (ROE) is one of the most favored metrics of investors. It is a profitability ratio that measures earnings generated by a company from its equity. Investors can follow the ROE trend in companies and compare this to historical or industry benchmarks to pick a winning stock.

However, stepping beyond the basic ROE and analyzing it at an advanced level could lead to even better returns. Here is where the DuPont analysis comes into play. It is an analytical method that examines three major elements – operating management, management of assets and the capital structure – related to the financial condition of a company. Below we show how DuPont breaks down ROE into its different components:

ROE = Net Income/Equity

Net Income / Equity = (Net Income / Sales) * (Sales / Assets) * (Assets / Equity)

ROE = Profit Margin * Asset Turnover Ratio * Equity Multiplier

The screener yields winning stocks like MYR Group MYRG, Blue Bird BLBD, Guardian Pharmacy Services GRDN, Ubiquiti UI and Everus Construction Group Inc. ECG.

Why Use DuPont?

Although one can’t play down the importance of normal ROE calculation, the fact remains that it doesn’t always provide a complete picture. The DuPont analysis, on the other hand, allows investors to assess the elements that play a dominant role in any change in ROE. It can help investors to segregate companies with higher margins from those with high turnover. For example, high-end fashion brands generally survive on a high margin as compared with retail goods, which rely on higher turnover.

In fact, it also sheds light on the company’s leverage status, which can go a long way in selecting stocks poised for gains. A lofty ROE could be due to the overuse of debt. Thus, the strength of a company can be misleading if it has a high debt load.

So, an investor confined solely to an ROE perspective may be confused if he or she has to judge between two stocks of equal ratios. This is where DuPont analysis wins over and spots the better stock.

Investors can simply do this analysis by taking a look at the company’s financials.However, looking at the financial statements of each company separately can be a tedious task. Screening tools like Zacks Research Wizard can come to your rescue and help you shortlist the stocks that look impressive with a DuPont analysis.

Screening Parameters

• Asset Turnover Ratio more than or equal to 2: It allows an investor to assess management’s efficiency in using assets to drive sales.

• Equity Multiplier between 1 and 3: It’s an indication of how much debt the company uses to finance its assets.
